content.text: If you use any external values inside your closure, Swift *captures* them – stores them alongside the closure, so they can be modified even if they don’t exist any more.
Right now we have a `travel()` function that returns a closure, and the returned closure accepts a string as its only parameter and returns nothing:
We can call `travel()` to get back the closure, then call that closure freely:

This calls `makeTrivialEncrypter()` with a parameter when it expects none, and returns a closure that uses a parameter when it doesn't have one.
